question: Should OpenClaw accept currentTokenCount plus these SDK token-budget helper exports as a stable public ContextEngine/plugin SDK contract now, or fold the token-budget signal into the broader assemble metadata RFC #82137?
rationale: The patch changes public plugin API and SDK exports that third-party context engines may compile against while the broader assemble metadata design remains unsettled, so automation cannot decide the permanent contract shape.

options.title: Accept Narrow Contract After Fixes
options.body: Approve currentTokenCount as a separate backward-compatible API after the implementation, generated artifacts, and real behavior proof are repaired.

options.title: Fold Into RFC #82137
options.body: Pause or close this branch and land token counts together with the broader provenance/internal-event assemble metadata design.

options.title: Keep Helpers Private For Now
options.body: Keep the assemble field if desired but remove or defer public SDK helper exports until maintainers settle the plugin API surface.

recommendation.title: Accept Narrow Contract After Fixes
recommendation.body: Approve currentTokenCount as a separate backward-compatible API after the implementation, generated artifacts, and real behavior proof are repaired.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned and have the strongest recent merged history on the context-engine budget path affected by this API decision.
